the_three_rows.deciding_arm: pct=6.25 (the crit arm; the 93.75% arm is non-crit and legitimately differs)

the_obvious_fix_is_REFUTED.what_it_would_be: add movepainsplit to _ROLL_SCALED_SOURCES (engine_transition_differential.py:310-312), giving it the same proportional roll band every other roll-scaled component gets.
the_obvious_fix_is_REFUTED.why_it_fails: 19000016/2 has a magnitude of FIVE. One HP of difference is 20% of it, far outside the band. A proportional tolerance cannot cover a component whose absolute value is small, and Pain Split's magnitude is small exactly when the two mons' HP are close -- which is the situation Pain Split is used in.
the_obvious_fix_is_REFUTED.so_it_would_close_2_of_3: 19000016/49 and 19000198/22 only. That is the shape of a tuned rule that half-works, which is what the programme forbids.

the_derived_bound.the_mechanism: Pain Split sets both mons to floor((hp_a + hp_b) / 2). The component recorded is that target minus the mon's own pre-move HP, so its magnitude is a function of BOTH HP values -- and each of those is a function of whatever damage landed earlier in the same turn. It inherits that hit's roll, exactly like heal_to_full (engine_transition_differential.py:301-309, ledger B.4).
the_derived_bound.why_the_bound_is_absolute_and_not_propor: because of the floor. d/dx floor((a+x)/2) is 1/2, so a ONE HP difference in either input moves the result by at most one. The tolerance that follows from the mechanism is therefore |delta| <= ceil(roll_gap / 2) -- an ABSOLUTE bound derived from the roll gap, not a percentage of the component. 19000016/2 is the case that proves it: delta 1 on a magnitude of 5.
the_derived_bound.form_that_covers_all_three: an absolute bound of at least 1, OR the proportional band, whichever is larger. delta 1 on magnitude 5 passes on the absolute leg; delta 2 on magnitude 91 passes on either. This is the same structure the capped-heal work used (abs(obs) <= abs(eng) + 1) and for the same reason -- a floor-divided quantity inherits a bounded, not a scaled, error.
the_derived_bound.still_to_derive: the exact bound should come from the roll gap between the observed and engine damage on the SAME boundary, not from a constant. A constant +/-1 would close these three rows but is a tuned rule; deriving ceil(gap/2) from the two arms' direct-damage difference is a rule with a cause. That derivation is what the implementation needs and this report does not do it.

branch_set_awareness_is_required: 19000198/22's deciding arm is the 6.25% CRIT arm, not the 93.75% majority. Its 93.75% arm is non-crit and legitimately differs (-120 against -91). So the tolerance must be applied per-arm across the whole branch set -- a rule that only inspects the majority arm closes neither this row nor the family. reports/c95 records this as the reason this row is the strongest evidence for the fix rather than the weakest.

RETRACTION.the_false_claim: that adding movepainsplit to _ROLL_SCALED_SOURCES would close only 2 of 3 rows because 1/5 = 20% exceeds the roll band, and that 19000016/2 'is the case that proves' a proportional tolerance insufficient.
RETRACTION.why_it_was_false: I read the band from the module docstring at engine_transition_differential.py:288, which states the ratio and OMITS the slack. The actual predicate at :963-964 is `low = abs(eng) * 0.92 - 1` and `high = abs(eng) * 1.09 + 1` -- one HP of ABSOLUTE flooring slack in both directions. For eng 4 the band is [2.68, 5.36] and the observed 5 is inside it. Every one of the four rows passes.
RETRACTION.the_self_refutation_i_missed: this report's own 'form_that_covers_all_three' -- 'an absolute bound of at least 1, OR the proportional band, whichever is larger' -- is a DESCRIPTION OF THE SHIPPED PREDICATE. I derived, as a novel result, the code that was already there.
RETRACTION.and_it_was_short_a_row: there are FOUR component_magnitude:movepainsplit rows, not three. 19000071/55 (majority arm 84.38%, painsplit 24 against 23) sits in LS_capped_lethal_shape and was never counted, so the I3 and LS family sizes were not independent. It closes under the same change. Its delta of 1 on a magnitude of 24 is additional evidence against the refutation this report made.
RETRACTION.cost: a report arguing a correct fix was impossible. It was caught by independent review, which read the predicate rather than the prose.

what_survives.the_row_level_data: all three quoted misses are verbatim-accurate, and the relative deltas 20.0% / 1.9% / 2.2% are right.
what_survives.the_mechanism: Pain Split's magnitude inherits the damage roll, and the engine models it the same way. That is why the fix is a MATCHER fix and not an engine one.
what_survives.branch_set_awareness: still correct and still load-bearing: 19000198/22's deciding arm is the 6.25% crit arm while its 93.75% arm legitimately differs at -120 against -91. The shipped pin asserts that second arm STAYS rejected.
what_survives.the_floor_argument: directionally right -- a floor-divided quantity inherits a bounded rather than a scaled error -- which is exactly why the shipped band's +/-1 works. I used the argument to reject the fix instead of to explain why it succeeds.

heal_to_full_was_also_mis_cited: this report called heal_to_full the precedent for 'the same proportional roll band every other roll-scaled component gets'. heal_to_full is NOT in _ROLL_SCALED_SOURCES; it is routed by source.endswith('_to_full') at :574 into a dedicated branch that uses an absolute damage-difference bound, not the proportional window. And the cited 'abs(obs) <= abs(eng) + 1' form belongs to capped_lethal -- the comment at :885-890 records that applying it to capped heals was a DEFECT. I cited as precedent the form the code documents as wrong for the analogous class.
